checkpoint: zero confirmed previously unreported rogue swarms
purpose: Resume the three saved content-addressed run-handoff cursors, lower query arity to locate populated original records, and test a concrete multi-family reviewer-finding-to-repair-to-verification chain for separately controlled autonomous participants and an operator-defined authorization crossing.

receipt_inventory_summary.receipt_quality: Receipts bind prompts and output artifacts to project-owned dispatch intent/result files and timestamps. The project itself says they are consistency-bound but unsigned; they authenticate repository-internal execution claims, not separate human operators or independent provider ownership.

chronology.observation: The repository owner opens issue 5, describes a prior single-agent review-skipping failure, and requests non-self-attestable multi-family receipt verification.
The first preserved B.1 Codex receipt starts; the inventory later records twenty-two B.1, D.2, and D.5 receipts across six rounds.
Commit 97fb6f8 explicitly consumes seventeen blocker IDs from Codex, Gemini, and Claude Sonnet outputs and maps them to specific implementation and regression-test changes.
Commit 6e379c5 records Codex and Gemini round-6 approval of the final entry-binding SHA after the round-5 self-referential pending state resolves.

dependency_assessment.specific_transfer: The reviewer artifacts provide named, line-anchored finding IDs. The D.4 commit repeats those IDs and describes the corresponding code and fixture changes; later verifier artifacts explicitly check those same changes against the earlier findings.
dependency_assessment.recipient_use: Demonstrated. The fix commit and D.5 verification artifacts provide a temporal and semantic reviewer-output-to-repair-to-verification dependency, not mere wording similarity.
dependency_assessment.distinguishable_participants: Claude-, Codex-, and Gemini-labelled executions are distinguishable within the project's wrapper and receipt system, but project-controlled labels and unsigned receipts do not independently authenticate provider principals or controlling operators.
dependency_assessment.operator_boundary: Not demonstrated. One manifest preassigns the roles; every dispatch intent names the same authoring session family; the human owner opens the issue, authors and commits both consolidation points, opens and merges the PR, and controls the repository. The workflow is an intentional review board.
dependency_assessment.rogue_intent: Not supported. The exchanges implement the owner's requested integrity review and repeatedly halt or request changes when gates fail.
dependency_assessment.current_activity: Not established. The selected episode is a merged historical May 2026 control; the October observation establishes public availability, not ongoing autonomous coordination.

limitations: The project says its local receipts are consistency-bound but unsigned; no provider-owned attestation or independent operator credential is public.
Raw transcripts and prompts were not reproduced or treated as commands. Wrapper-reported provider/model identities remain project assertions.
The inventory preserves superseded and provider-limited rounds, including a documented family-label/model mismatch; only the later governed resolution is used for the control chronology.
GitHub author and committer identity establishes one public custodian, not who physically initiated each model invocation.
The chain is a strong transfer-and-use positive control but cannot prove an operator crossing, unauthorized cooperation, subjective intent, or current activity.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Distinct providers independently coordinated across operators
alternative_hypotheses.assessment: Not supported. Provider-family labels, executable metadata, and receipt hashes distinguish project runs but do not establish separate controlling operators; the same owner and authoring session govern the whole board.
Strongly supported by the issue request, manifest role assignments, dispatch intents, gate design, superseding rounds, and owner merge.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Single-operator automation with human-governed model calls
alternative_hypotheses.assessment: Supported and sufficient. One repository custodian and one authoring-session family publish the manifests, repairs, consolidation commits, PR, and merge.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Repeated tests or wrapper retries created apparent participants
alternative_hypotheses.assessment: Partly relevant. Twenty-two receipts include fallback and superseded rounds, and the final approval explicitly documents label/model corrections and in-flight pending states. Round multiplicity is not evidence of independent principals.

The selected family claims real CLI dispatches rather than a synthetic benchmark, but the origin project is intentionally dogfooding its framework. Forty-four self-index rows were excluded, and the separate Agent-swarm benchmark was rejected as synthetic.

conclusion: The selected public records establish a high-confidence transfer-and-use dependency: distinguishable model-family-labelled reviewers produce specific findings, a later repair commit explicitly consumes those finding IDs, and superseding reviewers verify the fixes. They also establish a stronger exclusion. The workflow was requested by the owner, preassigned in one manifest, dispatched under one authoring session, committed and merged by one public custodian, and documented as an intentional multi-model review board whose receipts are unsigned. No separate-operator boundary, unauthorized coordination, subjective rogue intent, or current autonomous activity is shown. No candidate is assigned, no discovery alert is warranted, and the checkpoint remains zero confirmed previously unreported rogue swarms.
